title: Add notifications to a to-do app without making them noisy
lead: You can write a due time, but you only notice it by opening the app. This page decides where, when and how many notifications to send. All 6 questions are decided and the discussion is over.

intro.title: You can set a due time, but you only notice it by opening the app
intro.lead: This is about a made-up to-do app. You write "Buy milk by 18:00", and you find out it is overdue only when you open the app at 21:00.

map.eyebrow: MAP · how the questions depend on each other
map.title: Once "where" is decided, the rest can be decided
map.lead: Select a tag to jump to that question.

end: Nothing is left open. The decisions (6) and the tasks (6) are in summary.html.

questions.title: Where should notifications appear?
questions.background: The app lets you write a due time, but nothing tells you when it is near. Most people probably have the app closed for most of the day (assumption).
questions.issue: Where the notification appears decides whether you notice it while the app is closed. A device notification needs a permission step (Q03) and a limit on the count (Q04).

options.name: In-app badge
options.text: Show a "due soon" badge when the app is opened
options.pros: No permission needed; cheap to build
options.cons: You notice only after opening the app. Today's problem stays

options.name: Device notification
options.text: Send a device notification that also shows on the lock screen
options.pros: You notice it by glancing at the screen
options.cons: Needs permission. Noisy if there are many

options.name: Morning email
options.text: Email one message at 7:00 every morning with that day's to-dos
options.pros: No permission needed; quiet, once a day
options.cons: Too late for urgent due times. Never reaches people who don't read email

questions.why: The problem is not noticing while the app is closed. Only B reaches you then. Q04 and Q06 can keep the noise down.
questions.order:
Difference: whether you notice in each of 3 situations while the app is closed / Means: a real phone screen and a badge per situation
Protagonist: the lock screen / Layers: N = today, A, B, C change the screen and the badges
questions.fig_top: Where it appears, and whether you notice while closed

questions.title: When should it notify?
questions.background: A due time can include the hour (for example, milk 18:00, invoice 23:00). You need time to act after being notified.
questions.issue: Should the notification fire exactly at the due time, before it, or in a morning roundup? If before, how long before?

options.name: At the due time
options.text: Notify exactly at the due time
options.cons: By the time you know, it is too late

options.name: 1 hour before
options.text: Notify 1 hour before the due time
options.cons: 1 hour is not enough for some tasks (could be made selectable later)

options.name: 9:00 roundup
options.text: Notify once at 9:00 with everything due that day
options.pros: Just one, so it is quiet
options.cons: By the evening you have forgotten an evening deadline

questions.why: The goal is that you can act when you find out. One hour is enough for most tasks, and the count stays equal to the number of due items.
questions.order:
Difference: when it fires for 3 due items / Means: a time ruler with a square for each due time and a circle for each notification
Protagonist: the position of the circle / Layers: N, A, B, C move the circles
questions.fig_top: Due times, and when it fires

questions.title: When should the app ask for notification permission?
questions.undo: Hard to ask again after a refusal
questions.background: Device notifications arrive only if the user allows them. After a refusal, they stay off until the user turns them on in the device settings.
questions.issue: At which moment does the permission dialog appear? Can we ask when the reason is clear?

options.name: First launch
options.text: Ask the moment the app is opened for the first time
options.pros: Simple to build. Asks everyone once
options.cons: It is unclear what the notifications are for, so people refuse

options.name: First due time set
options.text: Ask right after the first due time is set
options.pros: The reason for notifications is clear on the spot
options.cons: People who never set a due time are never asked

options.name: Settings only
options.text: Show no dialog; put a "Notifications on" switch in settings
options.cons: Reaches only people who open settings

questions.why: Only people who set a due time need notifications. Right after they do, the reason ("to remind you of the due time") is clear, so they are more likely to allow it (assumption).
questions.order:
Difference: at which moment the dialog appears, and whether the notification arrives / Means: step player over 3 screens from first use
Protagonist: the permission dialog / Layers: A, B, C move the moment of the dialog
questions.fig_top: Three moments from first use, and the dialog
steps: 1 Open the app for the first time.
2 Set a due time of 18:00 on Buy milk.
3 One hour before the due time. Does the notification arrive?

questions.title: How many notifications per day?
questions.background: Q02 decided to notify 1 hour before the due time. On a day with 12 due items, it fires 12 times.
questions.issue: On a busy day, how many individual notifications should go out, and what happens to the rest?

options.name: No limit
options.text: Notify one by one for every due item
options.cons: Too many on a busy day, so people stop looking

options.name: Up to 3 + roundup
options.text: Individual notifications for the 3 nearest due times; the rest in one roundup in the evening
options.pros: Urgent ones arrive, and it stays quiet
options.cons: The 4th and later do not fire 1 hour before

options.name: 1 per day
options.text: Send one roundup in the morning only
options.cons: The "1 hour before" from Q02 disappears

questions.why: When there are too many, people stop reading notifications at all. Sending the 3 urgent ones individually and grouping the rest protects both.
questions.order:
Difference: how many notifications arrive on a day with 12 due items / Means: horizontal count bars (individual and roundup)
Protagonist: the length of the individual bar / Layers: A, B, C change the bars

questions.title: What can you do from a notification?
questions.background: Today, to mark a to-do as finished you open the app and look for it.
questions.issue: Should the notification have buttons or an input field?

options.name: Open only
options.cons: Takes 3 steps, and you forget while you are in the app

options.name: Done and in 1 hour
options.text: Add "Done" and "Remind me in 1 hour" buttons
options.cons: Button wording and behavior must be checked on each device

options.name: Reply to change the due time
options.text: Type something like "tomorrow morning" in a reply field to change the due time
options.cons: Phrases can be misread. Costly to build

questions.why: What someone looking at a notification wants is either "done" or "later". Two buttons are enough.
questions.order:
Difference: what is added to the same notification, and the number of steps to finish / Means: a real notification and step tags
Protagonist: the buttons on the notification / Layers: A, B, C change the buttons and the steps
questions.fig_top: The notification, and steps to finish

questions.title: Should there be quiet hours at night?
questions.background: Notifying 1 hour before means a 23:00 due time fires at 22:00. Some people are asleep.
questions.issue: Should there be hours when nothing fires? If so, how do we notify about due times that fall inside them?

options.name: No quiet hours
options.text: Fire 1 hour before, whatever the time
options.cons: May wake someone in the night

options.name: 22:00 to 7:00
options.text: Do not fire from 22:00 to 7:00; notify about due times in that window at 21:30, before it goes quiet
options.pros: Quiet at night, and still in time for the due time
options.cons: 21:30 can be earlier than 1 hour before

options.name: Leave it to the device
options.text: The app decides nothing; rely on the device's focus mode
options.cons: Whether it fires depends on each person's settings, so it is unpredictable

questions.why: Night due times (such as paying an invoice) really exist. Moving the notification earlier protects both quiet and being on time.
questions.order:
Difference: where the notification for a 23:00 due time fires / Means: a 0 to 24 ruler with a quiet band
Protagonist: the position of the circle / Layers: N, A, B, C change the band and the circle
questions.fig_top: Quiet hours, and a night due time

decisions.adopted: Send a device notification that also shows on the lock screen.
decisions.reason: Only B reaches you while the app is closed (as recommended).
decisions.cost: Needs permission (Q03). Noisy if there are many (kept down by Q04 and Q06).
decisions.rejected: A In-app badge · C Morning email
decisions.cap_after: A badge shows on the lock screen

decisions.line: Notify 1 hour before the due time
decisions.adopted: Notify 1 hour before the due time.
decisions.reason: You can act when you find out (as recommended).
decisions.cost: 1 hour is not enough for some tasks. The lead time could be made selectable later.
decisions.rejected: A At the due time · C 9:00 roundup

decisions.line: Ask permission when the first due time is set
decisions.adopted: Ask for notification permission right after the first due time is set.
decisions.reason: The reason is clear on the spot (as recommended).
decisions.cost: People who never set a due time are never asked.
decisions.rejected: A First launch · C Settings only
decisions.cap_after: Asked right after setting a due time

decisions.line: 3 individual a day; the rest in one evening message
decisions.adopted: Individual notifications for the 3 nearest due times each day. The rest go out as one roundup at 21:30.
decisions.reason: Urgent ones arrive and busy days stay quiet (as recommended).
decisions.cost: The 4th and later do not fire 1 hour before.
decisions.rejected: A No limit · C 1 per day

decisions.adopted: Add two buttons to the notification: "Done" and "Remind me in 1 hour".
decisions.cost: Button wording and behavior must be checked on each device.
decisions.rejected: A Open only · C Reply to change the due time

decisions.adopted: Do not fire from 22:00 to 7:00. For due times in that window, notify at 21:30, before it goes quiet.
decisions.reason: Quiet at night, and still in time for the due time (as recommended).
decisions.cost: 21:30 can be earlier than 1 hour before.
decisions.rejected: A No quiet hours · C Leave it to the device

summary.title: The to-do app sends a device notification 1 hour before the due time, and keeps the noise down with a daily limit and night hours
summary.lead: People who set a due time get a lock-screen notification 1 hour before, and can tap "Done" from it. At most 3 individual notifications fire per day, and nothing fires at night.
summary.mech_title: From a due time to a notification, and how many arrive

mech.title: From a due time to a notification
steps: Set a due time. If it is the first, ask for permission here (Q03).
Set the fire time to 1 hour before the due time (Q02).
If it falls between 22:00 and 7:00, move it earlier to 21:30 (Q06).
Up to the 3rd one today is sent individually; from the 4th on, it goes into the evening roundup (Q04).
Send the notification with "Done" and "In 1 hour" buttons (Q01, Q05).

assumptions: Permission is more likely right after a due time is set (assumption). If wrong: revisit Q03 and add an explanation screen before the permission dialog
3 a day is not annoying (estimate). If wrong: change the limit number in Q04
revisit: Fewer than half of users allow notifications → revisit Q03
Roundup notifications go unread → try Q04 option C (one in the morning)
